season-2.headline: Week 6: Eight More Unbeatens Fall, San Diego State Closes In on Alabama, and UCF and Queens Crash the Field
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Eighteen days and 1,805 games are in, 312 of them since the last bracket. Last week I told you the unbeaten list had just had the worst three days of its life. It had another bad three: eight more teams lost their first game, taking the list from 27 on Day 15 to 19 today. Here is the week, what mattered in it, and what didn't.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Four results moved the bracket. Liberty won 71-69 at Virginia. UCF beat North Carolina 90-70 and then Tennessee 71-59. Queens won 95-75 at Kansas State. And Cornell, which had lost 108-56 at Texas on Day 16, turned around on Day 17 and beat New Hampshire 74-66 on the road. By my ratings that was the biggest upset of the week, a 24-point miss.

Everything else that looked dramatic on the scoreboard was chalk or noise. San Diego State beat Radford 119-35, an 84-point margin, which is the largest in league history (the old record was 74). It moved the Aztecs exactly zero seed lines, because they were already on the top line. Michigan St. went to Arizona and won 79-77, and it is still on my Next Four Out list. Butler lost 90-87 in overtime at Akron and slid only two lines, to a 10. A win over a team I don't rate barely moves a rating, and that is why the loudest results of the week were the quietest on the bracket.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama (10-0) is the overall No. 1 seed for the sixth straight week, with a 110-73 win at Boston College on Day 16 as its only game. The Crimson Tide are scoring 106.8 and allowing 61.8, a margin of 45.0 points a game, the best in the country, and they are rated 46.3. San Diego State (9-0, rated 44.0) is right behind, and this week it is close enough that I want to be honest about it. On my Board, which scores every team's resume, Alabama is at 51.1 and San Diego State is at 50.3. The Aztecs have a win over a top-25 team, a win over a team rated 26th to 50th, and a schedule rated 5.3. Alabama has no win over a top-25 team, one over a team rated 26th to 50th, and a schedule rated 1.3. The rating gap is 2.3 points. Once the resume is added, Alabama's lead shrinks to 0.8, because San Diego State has the better wins and the harder schedule.

Here is the stat that bothers me. Only 19 teams in the country have beaten a team I rate in the top 25, and between them they own 20 such wins. Alabama is not one of the 19. Cornell, which is 8-7 and rated 128th, is. I am not saying Cornell is better than Alabama. I am saying the best team in the country has never been tested by a top-25 team, and nobody knows what happens when it is. On current ratings that first test comes on Day 23 at Vanderbilt, the 14th-rated team, because Tennessee, where the Tide play on Day 21, is rated 47th.

I'm keeping Alabama on the overall No. 1 line because a +45 margin is a real thing, and I'm saying out loud that it's no longer a comfortable call. The next three days of conference play will decide it: San Diego State plays at Grand Canyon on Day 21 and at Utah St. on Day 22, two games against teams rated in the top 60, and the second is against the fifth-best team in the country. Alabama's first two are at Tennessee and at Vanderbilt. I would rather have the Aztecs' two days than the Tide's.

Gonzaga (10-0) and Texas (8-0) hold the other two top spots. Gonzaga beat VCU 89-73 and won 81-75 at Georgetown, which gives it one win over a top-25 team and one over a team rated 26th to 50th. Texas beat Cornell 108-56 and Richmond 111-74, and it owns two wins over top-25 teams, Iowa St. and Texas Tech, more than anyone else in the country. That is the whole case for Texas on the top line over Seton Hall, which is 9-0 after a 92-81 win over Virginia and leads the 2 seeds with Utah St., Florida and Florida State.

THE WEEK THE UNBEATEN LIST LOST EIGHT MORE
Arizona lost 82-73 at home to Vanderbilt on Day 16 and then 79-77 at home to Michigan St. on Day 17, so it didn't just lose its perfect record, it lost two in two days. North Carolina lost 90-70 at UCF. VCU lost 89-73 at Gonzaga. Virginia lost 71-69 at home to Liberty. St. Louis lost 86-69 at Pepperdine. Chattanooga lost 100-65 at Kansas. East Tennessee State lost 70-58 at Stonehill. Southeastern Louisiana lost 81-62 at home to Fresno State. Nineteen teams are left, and 18 of them are in my field. The exception is West Georgia.

Last week I told you to watch VCU at Gonzaga, Gonzaga at Georgetown and Virginia at Seton Hall. All three went the way the ratings said. By my rough math last week VCU had about a 6% chance at Gonzaga and Virginia about 26% at Seton Hall, and neither came through. There was an irony in the Seton Hall game: Virginia had already lost at home to Liberty two days earlier, so the game I had billed as one perfect record ending turned out to be a 7-1 team losing to a 9-0 one. Virginia went 0-2 on the week and slides from a 3 seed to a 4. North Carolina does the same.

THE FALLEN
Tennessee is the biggest drop on the board. The Volunteers were a 6 seed last week, lost 56-55 at Penn State on Day 16 and 71-59 at UCF on Day 18, and are out of the field. They are 6-3 and rated 47th, down from 23rd. Kansas State goes from a 7 seed to a 12 after losing 95-75 to Queens at home on Day 16 (rated 52nd, down from 27th). Arizona goes from a 5 to a 10. New Hampshire (12-2) goes from a 4 to a 6 because of Cornell, and it is still the best team in America East by more than 16 rating points over Vermont. Grand Canyon won both of its games, finished 8-2, and is out of the field. That one needs explaining, so it gets a paragraph below.

THE RISERS
UCF is the biggest riser in the country. The Knights were on my Next Four Out list a week ago and are now a 7 seed. UCF (8-1) went from 5-1 to 8-1 in three days with wins over North Carolina, Tennessee and Kansas City and is rated 33rd, up from 71st. Queens (8-1) was on that same list and is now the ASUN's automatic bid and a 10 seed. It went 3-0 with the win at Kansas State and rose from 72nd to 34th, a gain of 8.1 rating points, the largest of any team in the top 100. Liberty goes from first four out to a 12 seed with the win at Virginia. Pepperdine, which beat St. Louis 86-69, goes from a 10 to a 7. Vanderbilt (9-1) goes from a 5 to a 3 after winning at Arizona. Bradley goes from an 8 to a 5.

THE AUTO-BIDS: NINE CHANGED HANDS
I pick each conference's automatic bid by best rating, not best record, and this week nine of the 31 changed. Queens takes the ASUN from West Georgia (18.7 to 15.3). Wisconsin takes the Big 10 from Illinois by 0.18 rating points, 18.81 to 18.63, with Iowa another half-point back at 18.08. Bradley takes the Missouri Valley from Valparaiso (25.1 to 21.1). UAB takes the American from Memphis (17.6 to 16.6), which drops Memphis out of the field. Sacramento State takes the Big Sky from Eastern Washington, New Orleans (10-0) takes the Southland from Southeastern Louisiana, Abilene Christian takes the WAC from Utah Valley, and Stonehill takes the Northeast from Le Moyne, which lost 44-43 at Montana State, a team rated 304th. And the Horizon's best-rated team is Oakland, which is 3-7. The league is 30-77 in non-conference games, the worst of any conference.

That produces the First Four's two 16-seed games: Abilene Christian (12-4) against Stonehill (5-6), and UNC Asheville (7-6) against Oakland (3-7). The four teams are a combined 27-23, and two of them, Stonehill and Oakland, are under .500.

THE LAST FOUR IN AND OUT
The last four in are Michigan, Nebraska, Purdue and East Tennessee State. Michigan is the last team in, and I should explain why Grand Canyon isn't. My Board has Grand Canyon ahead of Michigan by one hundredth of a point, 16.94 to 16.93, and I overruled it. Michigan is 9-1 against a schedule rated -0.5 with no bad losses. Grand Canyon is 8-2 against a schedule rated -3.4. If the Board is a coin flip, the record and the schedule break it. The first four out are Grand Canyon, Tennessee, Marquette and West Georgia. The next four out are Memphis, Michigan St., Chattanooga and Fresno State.

Michigan and Nebraska are in a First Four game that will have a rehearsal before it happens: Nebraska plays at Michigan on Day 21. And Wisconsin, the Big 10's auto-bid, visits Purdue on Day 23, which is a conference game between the league's automatic bid and a team in the First Four.

PATTERNS: WHAT THE WEEK TELLS US
The power leagues dominated everyone else again. In non-conference games this week the Big 10 went 22-5, the Big 12 20-7, the WCC 17-6, the Big East 14-5 and the Mountain West 11-3. The ACC was the one league in that group that didn't clean up, going 21-13, a .618 clip, with North Carolina's loss at UCF and Virginia's at home to Liberty in the middle of it. At the other end, the CAA went 3-16, the Big West 3-14, the Ohio Valley 4-16, the Big South 5-15 and the Atlantic 10 6-15. For the season the Big East has the best non-conference record at .760 (76-24), ahead of the Big 12 (.741), the SEC (.713), the Big 10 (.708), the Mountain West (.701) and the ACC (.681).

By average rating the order is the SEC (14.8), the Big East (12.8), the Mountain West (12.5), the Big 12 (12.2), the Big 10 (9.6) and the ACC (9.5). The Mountain West has passed the Big 12 for third, and the SEC slipped from 15.2 last week. The five power leagues have 34 of the 68 spots and 29 of the 37 at-large bids, up from 33 and 28. The Big 12 has the most bids with nine, with UCF the new one. The ACC has eight, the SEC six (down one, Tennessee), the Big 10 six (up one, Nebraska) and the Big East five. The Mountain West and the WCC have three each.

Home teams won 56.3% of their games this week (175-136), up from 52.2% on Days 13 to 15 and about where the season sits at 57.1%. Scoring fell to 69.4 points per team from 72.1 through Day 15. Forty-one of the 312 games were decided by three points or fewer, five went to overtime, including Akron over Butler and Marquette at Sacramento State, and 24 were decided by 40 or more.

The tiers are still sorting the league. Tier S teams went 32-8 this week and tier A teams 36-13, while tier D teams went 61-98 and tier F teams 43-98. The exceptions are the ones that make a bracket interesting. Bradley is a tier C program, is rated 25 points above where its tier says it should be, and is a 5 seed. Sacramento State is a tier F program at 9-3 and a 14 seed. And the other direction is ugly: Auburn, a tier A team, is 3-6 and rated 255th with six bad losses, 21.9 points below its tier. Kentucky is 5-3 with three bad losses and Houston is 6-3 and rated 127th. I had Kentucky in and Houston out in the preseason, and I'm going to take that as a win for the preseason.

One more number on the stack of numbers that don't match the records. The 25 best teams in my ratings are 212-20 on the season, a .914 clip, and only nine games all year have been between two top-25 teams. Two of them were this week: Gonzaga over Georgetown and Seton Hall over Virginia. That is why a team can be unbeaten and still not be tested. Arkansas, UAB and West Georgia are all unbeaten with zero wins over a team in the top 100. I have Arkansas on a 5 because its rating is 22nd, which is the one place this week I'm trusting the rating over the resume. UAB is a 13 and West Georgia is out.

THE HOT TAKES
Navy is an 8 seed, and I will defend it at the bar. The Midshipmen are 11-0, rated 30th, up from 43rd, and they have a win over a team rated 26th to 50th. The objection is the schedule, which is rated -4.0. The answer is that the rating already accounts for the schedule, and it still has Navy ahead of Pittsburgh, Miami and Colorado, all of whom I have on the 9 and 10 lines. In week 4 I wrote that a 30-0 Navy would be a 3 or 4 seed and not a 1. An 11-0 Navy on the 8 line is that same logic, one third of the way through.

West Georgia is out, and I'll live with it. It is 9-0, and my first four out include West Georgia because it is rated 54th, its schedule is rated -5.4, and it has not beaten a team in the top 100. New Orleans (10-0) is in only because Southeastern Louisiana lost, and it's a 14 seed. An unbeaten record against that schedule isn't a resume.

Pepperdine is the quiet resume of the year. It is tied with Gonzaga and San Diego State for the most wins over teams in the top 100, with five. If the committee rewarded volume of good wins, Pepperdine would be a 2 seed. It's a 7, because it also lost 53-50 at Cal State Northridge, and that loss is a bad loss on the Board.

THE HYPOTHETICAL: WHAT IF THE AUTO-BIDS WENT TO THE BEST RECORD?
My process picks each conference's automatic bid by rating. Suppose the committee used the best record instead. Eleven of the 31 conferences would give a different answer. An unbeaten Big 12 team, Baylor (8-0) or West Virginia (9-0), would be the league's bid instead of Texas Tech (8-1). Southern (8-1) would knock Arkansas-Pine Bluff (5-4) out of the SWAC slot, West Georgia (9-0) would take the ASUN, and the SoCon's slot would go to East Tennessee State or Chattanooga, both 10-1, instead of Wofford at 9-1. The rest are the MAC, the MAAC, the Northeast, the Big South, the Horizon, the Ohio Valley and the Big Sky.

The interesting part is what that does to the bubble. Queens (8-1, rated 34th) would be at-large fodder, and I think it would get in. Texas Tech would also be an at-large team, and a safe one. And Arkansas-Pine Bluff, a 5-4 team rated 95th that I have as a 16 seed, would be replaced by an 8-1 team that ratings say is 123rd. Records are not a bad way to pick a champion. They are a bad way to pick who deserves to be in, and that's the whole reason the ratings exist.

WHERE THIS IS HEADED
Days 19 and 20 are the last two non-conference days, and conference play starts on Day 21. Through Day 31 the schedule has eight games between teams that are unbeaten today: Arkansas at Texas on Day 22, Florida at Texas on Day 23, Iowa at Wisconsin on Day 24, Florida at Alabama and Texas at Arkansas on Day 27, Florida State at Duke and Seton Hall at Uconn on Day 28, and Pittsburgh at Florida State on Day 31. Four of the eight are SEC games and Texas is in three of them. Eleven different teams are in those games, which leaves eight unbeaten teams that don't face another unbeaten team before Day 32: Navy, Gonzaga, New Orleans, San Diego State, West Virginia, West Georgia, Baylor and UAB. Most of the next losses won't come from collisions at all. They'll come from games like East Tennessee State's at Stonehill, where the team with the better rating and the perfect record goes on the road and loses.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 19: Georgetown at Colorado. Day 20: Villanova at Florida and Valparaiso at Tennessee. Day 21: Alabama at Tennessee, San Diego State at Grand Canyon, Florida at Vanderbilt, Uconn at Marquette, San Francisco at Pepperdine and Nebraska at Michigan, the rehearsal for the First Four. Day 22: Arkansas at Texas, San Diego State at Utah St., Texas Tech at Kansas and Colorado at UCF. Day 23: Florida at Texas, Alabama at Vanderbilt, Wisconsin at Purdue, Liberty at New Mexico State and UCF at Texas Tech. Day 24: Florida State at Miami, West Virginia at Iowa St. and Arizona at Kansas State. Watch the top line, because the Alabama versus San Diego State question gets its first real data on Day 21 and Day 22. And watch the Big 10 bubble, because Michigan is the last team in and Nebraska plays there on Day 21.

season-2.headline: Week 7: Alabama's Lead Shrinks to 0.24, Four Automatic Bids Change Hands, and Georgetown Jumps to a 3
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Twenty-two days and 2,158 games are in, 353 of them since the last bracket. Last week eight unbeaten teams fell. This week four more did, and the list is down to 15. The story is not who lost, though. It is a lead at the top that has shrunk to a rounding error, and four conferences whose automatic bid changed hands.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama (11-0) is the overall No. 1 seed for the seventh straight week, and I will not pretend it is comfortable. The Tide won 100-55 at Tennessee on Day 21 and are rated 48.8. San Diego State (11-0, rated 47.8) went 2-0, beating Dartmouth 111-42 and winning 88-60 at Grand Canyon. On my Board, which adds wins and schedule to the rating, Alabama is at 54.32 and the Aztecs are at 54.08. Last week the gap was 0.8. It is now 0.24.

Last week I said the Tide had never beaten a top-25 team and that the first real test was Vanderbilt. Tennessee turned out to be a non-event: the Volunteers are 6-5, rated 60th, down from 47th, and also lost 92-80 to Valparaiso. Alabama has one top-25 win on the Board now. The Vanderbilt game on Day 23 is the one that matters, and the Commodores are coming off a 96-82 loss to Florida, so expect them to be annoyed. If Alabama loses, San Diego State is my No. 1 overall next week with no argument. If the Aztecs lose at Utah St. on Day 22, the Tide's lead is safe again. That is a lot of stakes for two games.

Gonzaga (11-0, rated 42.0) and Texas (11-0, rated 38.6) fill out the top line. Texas has two wins over top-25 teams and a Board score of 45.66, which is why it sits ahead of Florida (11-0, rated 34.1, Board 41.85) and Utah St. (10-1, rated 37.1). Florida beat Vanderbilt 96-82 and Villanova 77-64 and plays Texas on Day 23, which is the best game on the schedule that nobody will talk about because of Alabama. The 2 line is Florida, Utah St., Florida State and Seton Hall.

FOUR BIDS CHANGED HANDS
Automatic bids go to the best-rated team in each conference, not the team with the shiniest record. Four of them flipped.

VCU (10-1, rated 25.4) takes the A-10 from St. Louis (9-1, rated 23.7). Valparaiso (10-1, rated 26.7) takes the Missouri Valley from Bradley (10-1, rated 24.0), after beating Tennessee 92-80 and Northern Iowa 101-50. Valparaiso rose from 26th to 13th, which is the fourth-biggest rating jump in the country, and goes from a 6 seed to a 3. Bradley stays in as an at-large 5.

West Georgia (11-0, rated 20.2) takes the ASUN from Queens (10-1, rated 18.9). West Georgia is a Tier D team, it beat Nicholls State 81-41 and Stetson 97-37, and it is rated 34th, up from 54th. It goes from First Four Out to a 9 seed. Queens is a 9 as an at-large.

And Memphis (7-4, rated 21.3) takes the American from UAB (11-0, rated 18.9). I know that will annoy you. Memphis has four losses and the rating says it is 2.4 points better, because it has played a schedule rated 6.1 and UAB has played one rated -3.6. Memphis is a 10 seed, UAB is a 9, and the two play on Day 23, which will decide the bid for real.

RISERS
Georgetown is my biggest riser, up 9.0 rating points, from 21st to 9th. The Hoyas (9-2) beat Colorado 103-64, Buffalo 103-45 and Providence 81-69, and carry a schedule rated 7.1. They go from a 7 to a 3.

Missouri (9-2) goes from a 5 to a 3 with two 97-65 wins, over Iona and Texas A&M. Pepperdine goes from a 7 to a 4. The Waves (9-2) are rated 17th, up from 27th, after an 84-53 win over San Francisco. VCU is a 5, up from an 8, after beating Georgia State 97-37 and Rhode Island 104-53. Marquette is back in the field as a 12 after beating Uconn 79-50. Fresno State, on my Next Four Out list a week ago, comes in as a 13.

FALLERS
Four teams that were in last week are out. Colorado (8-3) lost 103-64 to Georgetown and 87-80 to Kansas. Villanova (7-4) lost 77-64 to Florida and 83-73 to Butler. Nebraska (7-4) lost 93-79 at Nevada, a 14-point upset by the ratings, and 77-73 to Michigan. Purdue (9-2) won twice, and still falls out, because its Board score of 17.59 is 0.35 behind East Tennessee State, the last team in. It is First Four Out, and it is the first call to argue with me about.

Last week's 3 seeds all slid. Baylor (11-1) lost 75-73 at BYU, a 15.6-point upset by the ratings, and goes from a 3 to a 5. Duke (10-1) lost 62-59 to Kentucky, an expected miss of 14.7, and goes from a 3 to a 6. Vanderbilt (9-2) lost by 14 to Florida and goes from a 3 to a 7. Uconn lost 79-50 to Marquette and slides from a 5 to an 8. West Virginia lost 66-51 to Cincinnati, a team that is 6-6, and falls from an 8 to the First Four.

THE UPSETS THAT MEANT NOTHING
Northern Colorado beat Idaho State 78-75. By the ratings that was a 24.7-point upset, the biggest of the week, and it moves nobody in my bracket. Georgia Southern's 71-61 win over Syracuse (22.6 points) and Northwestern's 76-68 win at Ohio St. (18.5) are the same. I stopped counting those as news a few weeks ago. A team outside the field beating another team outside the field does not change a seed.

THE SCOREBOARD LIE
Arizona went 4-0 this week, beating UC Davis 71-59 and St. John's 71-65, and TCU twice. It is still in the First Four, as an 11, because it is rated 55th and its wins were over teams that don't register. NC State (10-1) is the same story: it beat Radford 72-68 and SMU 92-63, and is rated 58th. A 10-1 record on a schedule rated -4.2 is flattering. Same for Navy (13-0), which is a 10 and rated 48th. It has played a schedule rated -5.7 and its week was a 70-34 win over Central Connecticut State and a 59-52 win over Loyola (MD). I am keeping it in because it has not lost, but I won't pretend it is a top-40 team.

WHAT IS BIG AND WHAT ISN'T
Big: Georgetown, Valparaiso, West Georgia and Memphis. All four moved because their ratings moved, not because of their records. Not big: the unbeaten list shrinking. Duke, West Virginia, Uconn and Baylor losing is fine; none of them was a top-line team. And Days 22 and 23 for Alabama and San Diego State may be the only thing that matters this week.

A HYPOTHETICAL
Say Alabama loses at Vanderbilt and San Diego State wins at Utah St. San Diego State becomes the No. 1 overall seed and the Tide fall behind it on the Board, with Gonzaga close behind. That is not a prediction. It is the arithmetic of a 0.24 gap.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 22: San Diego State at Utah St., Texas Tech at Kansas, Arkansas at Texas. Day 23: Alabama at Vanderbilt, Florida at Texas, UAB at Memphis, Wisconsin at Purdue, Liberty at New Mexico State. Day 24: Iowa at Wisconsin, Florida State at Miami, Baylor at Texas Tech. The one I would circle is Day 24's Iowa at Wisconsin, two 10-0 teams that cannot both leave undefeated.

One last note. The new engine that caps team strength and individual stats applies from the next game played, not the ones in this bracket. Every result above was played under the old rules, so I have no way to know yet how much this changes the standings. I will tell you next week.

season-2.headline: Week 8: San Diego State Takes the No. 1 Overall, Arkansas Wins at Texas and Gets a 5, and Purdue Proves Me Wrong
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Twenty-four days and 2,619 games are in, 461 of them since the last bracket. Seven more teams lost their perfect records and the unbeaten list is down to eight. One of the seven was Alabama, and that changes the top of the bracket for the first time in seven weeks.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Vanderbilt 73, Alabama 66. Arkansas won 83-79 at Texas. Fresno State won 71-63 at Utah St. Memphis beat UAB 95-84 in overtime. Purdue went 3-0, including a 66-49 win over Wisconsin.

Not big: Bowling Green beat Ohio 64-62, a 35.7-point upset by my ratings and the biggest of the week. Northern Iowa won 77-75 at Bradley, a 31.1-point miss. Both are funny. Only one moved a seed line, and that was Bradley's.

NEW NO. 1 OVERALL: SAN DIEGO STATE
Last week I wrote: "Say Alabama loses at Vanderbilt and San Diego State wins at Utah St. San Diego State becomes the No. 1 overall seed." I called it a hypothetical. It was a forecast. The Aztecs won 84-55 at Utah St. on Day 22, then beat Air Force 102-57 and Wyoming 108-68. They are 14-0 and rated 47.4.

Alabama lost 73-66 at Vanderbilt on Day 23 and then won 83-73 at Georgia. The Tide's rating fell from 48.8 to 43.3. On the Board, San Diego State is at 55.17 and Alabama is at 48.25. Last week the gap was 0.24. Now it is nearly seven points. That's not a race anymore.

The Aztecs are the No. 1 overall seed in the East. Alabama keeps a 1 seed in the South, and Texas and Gonzaga hold the other two.

Texas is the interesting one. It lost 83-79 at home to Arkansas on Day 22, then beat Florida 94-75 and Kentucky 92-62. It has three wins over top-25 teams, more than anyone in the country, and a Board score of 46.14. Gonzaga (13-0) has not lost but has two top-25 wins and a schedule rated 1.9. I think Texas has the better case. That's why the Longhorns are third and Gonzaga fourth.

THE ARKANSAS PROBLEM
Arkansas is 13-0 and went into Texas and won. It is a 5 seed. Let me defend that before you set something on fire.

The Razorbacks are rated 19th. The Texas win is their only win over a top-50 team, and their schedule is rated 0.6. Iowa is the same kind of team: 13-0, rated 21st, a schedule of 0.7. Iowa gets a 4 because it has a Q1 win and a Q2 win and just beat Wisconsin 84-73. Arkansas gets the chance to fix this quickly: Missouri visits on Day 25 and Texas on Day 27. If Arkansas wins both, it is a 2 seed next week and I'll apologise in print.

FOUR BIDS, TWO JUDGMENT CALLS
Iowa takes the Big 10's automatic bid from Wisconsin, which lost 66-49 to Purdue and 84-73 to Iowa in two days. Wisconsin falls from a 6 to a 9.

Then come the calls. I have been giving automatic bids to the best-rated team in each league. From here on, when two teams are within about a point, the standings and the head-to-head decide it. Two leagues qualify this week.

Big 12: Kansas (13-1, 4-0) over Texas Tech (12-2, 3-1). The ratings are 1.1 points apart, and Kansas beat the Red Raiders 90-77 on Day 22. Kansas goes from a 5 to a 3.

ASUN: Queens (13-1, 4-0) over West Georgia (13-1, 3-1). The ratings are 0.29 apart, and West Georgia lost 75-68 to North Alabama, a team rated 156th. They play on Day 27 at Queens, and that game settles it.

For the record, Memphis keeps the American and earned it this time. Last week I said the UAB game would decide the bid for real. Memphis won 95-84 in overtime at home and is 4-0 in the league. It goes from a 10 to a 7.

GRADING LAST WEEK
Right: the No. 1 overall flip, and Memphis. Half right: I told you to circle Iowa at Wisconsin because two 10-0 teams could not both stay unbeaten. Wisconsin solved that a day early by losing at Purdue.

Wrong: Purdue. I left the Boilermakers out by 0.35 Board points and called them the first team to argue with me about. They went 3-0, beat Wisconsin by 17 and Michigan St. twice, and lead the Big 10 at 4-0. They're an 11 seed now and deserve better than that soon. Also wrong: "Navy is not a top-40 team" was me being generous. The Midshipmen are 15-0 and rated 52nd.

MOVERS
The biggest jump is Fresno State, from a 13 to a 6. The Bulldogs beat New Mexico 79-52 and won at Utah St. They're 3-0 in the Mountain West and rated 28th, up from 38th. Vanderbilt goes from a 7 to a 4 on the Alabama win. Iowa goes from an 8 to a 4. Massachusetts goes from a 14 to a 9. The Minutemen are 10-3 and rated 29th, and they beat Ohio 93-71 and Akron 91-57.

Going the other way: Duke lost 79-65 at Georgia Tech, a 3-10 team and a 21.8-point miss, and falls from a 6 to a 10. North Carolina lost 76-74 at Notre Dame and falls from a 3 to a 6. Bradley falls from a 5 to an 8. Pepperdine lost 74-52 at Pacific and falls from a 4 to a 7. UCF lost three straight, to Colorado, Texas Tech and Oklahoma State, and falls from an 8 to a 12. One more loss and it's out.

Utah St. stays a 2 seed and I'm uneasy about it. It lost twice at home in three days, by 29 to San Diego State and by 8 to Fresno State. It is still rated seventh. It is the shakiest 2 seed I have put in this bracket.

IN AND OUT
In: Purdue, Villanova, Pacific and Longwood. Villanova swept Uconn, 66-57 and 85-64, and beat St. John's 75-73. Pacific (12-2) is 4-0 in the WCC and won that 74-52 game over Pepperdine.

Out: Liberty, Arizona, East Tennessee State and UNC Asheville. Liberty lost 73-71 to Middle Tennessee and 78-75 at New Mexico State, and now has two bad losses. Arizona lost 76-73 at home to BYU. East Tennessee State lost to The Citadel and UNC Greensboro and has three losses to teams outside my top 100. UNC Asheville is out because Longwood takes the Big South bid on rating, 4.7 to 2.2. Both are unbeaten in the league, and this is the one call this week I'd happily lose.

THE BUBBLE
Last four in: West Georgia, Pacific, Butler and San Francisco. First Four Out: Liberty, Arizona, Grand Canyon, Nebraska. Next Four Out: San Jose State, Chattanooga, Colorado, Syracuse.

Hot take: Pacific over Liberty is the right call, and it isn't close. Liberty is rated higher, but it has lost two straight and has two bad losses. Pacific has won the games in front of it, including a 22-point beating of a team I had as a 4 seed a week ago. I'll take the team that is winning its league over the one losing at home to Middle Tennessee.

THE PATTERN NOBODY ASKED FOR, EXCEPT THE COMMISSIONER
All 461 games since the last bracket were played under the new ceiling, and you can see it. Over Days 23 and 24, Tier S teams went 34-14. Last week they went 44-5. Games decided by 40 or more fell from 36 in 353 games to 18 in 316. The two biggest upsets of the week, by 35.7 and 31.1 points, were bigger than anything last week. The top ratings came down: Alabama lost 5.1 points, Gonzaga 3.7 and Utah St. 2.7. Home teams won 62.0%, and nine games went to overtime.

My read: nobody is a lock anymore, including San Diego State. That's the point of the change, and it makes my job harder in the best way.

A HYPOTHETICAL
Say the committee only counted conference games. Missouri (4-0), Kansas (4-0), Georgetown (4-0), VCU (4-0) and Valparaiso (4-0) would look like 1 and 2 seeds, and Florida, at 2-2, would be a 4. It's a silly way to seed a tournament, but here's the real point: Florida has lost two of four in the SEC and I still have it on the 2 line on the strength of its non-conference results. That probably won't last.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 25: Missouri at Arkansas, Marquette at Seton Hall, West Virginia at Kansas. Day 26: Missouri at Alabama, Kansas at Baylor. Day 27: Florida at Alabama, Texas at Arkansas, Utah St. at San Diego State, West Georgia at Queens, Michigan at Purdue. Day 28: Florida State at Duke, Texas at Vanderbilt, Baylor at Kansas. Day 29: Pepperdine at Gonzaga.

Arkansas has Missouri and Texas at home in three days, so that's my week. Win both and the 5 seed was a crime. Split, and it was about right.

season-2.headline: Week 9: Alabama Beats Missouri and Florida, Seven Teams Fall Out, and the Ceiling Grows Teeth
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Twenty-seven days and 3,101 games are in, 482 of them since the last bracket. The unbeaten list went from eight to four: San Diego State (17-0), Gonzaga (16-0), Seton Hall (16-0) and Iowa (15-0). Arkansas, Florida State, Navy and New Orleans are off it, and two of those four lost to teams that had no business beating them.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Alabama beat Missouri 88-72 and Florida 82-59 on back-to-back days. Arkansas split its two big home games. Kansas went 3-0 and is 7-0 in the Big 12. Queens beat West Georgia 73-70 and settled the ASUN. Seven teams fell out of the field.

Not big, even though it was loud: Bowling Green won 71-68 at Massachusetts, a 41.7-point upset by my ratings, bigger than anything last week. Wake Forest, 5-12, beat Florida State 76-61, a 37.4-point miss. Portland, 4-13, beat Pacific 80-60. They moved teams. None of them changed who's good.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State stays the No. 1 overall seed. The Aztecs beat Grand Canyon 77-55, won 75-66 at Wyoming, and beat Utah St. 78-65 for the second time in six days. They are at 54.77 on the Board.

Alabama is second at 49.63, and it had the best week in the country. Last week the Tide had one top-25 win. Now they have three, after beating Missouri and Florida by a combined 39 points. The gap to San Diego State is 5.1, down from nearly seven. The next real chance for it to close is the Aztecs' trip to UNLV on Day 30.

Gonzaga (16-0) won three road games by 32, 14 and 35 and stays on the top line. Texas keeps the fourth 1 seed, and I owe you the argument. The Longhorns lost 78-71 at Arkansas on Day 27, so the Razorbacks have now beaten them twice. Texas is 14-2 with three top-25 wins and a schedule rated 8.2, and its Board score is 43.02. Seton Hall is next at 39.26 with one top-25 win. Arkansas is at 31.29. Beating a team twice doesn't make you the better team over a whole season, and Arkansas's schedule is rated 4.5 to Texas's 8.2. Texas stays. If Texas loses at Vanderbilt on Day 28 or at Missouri on Day 30, it won't stay.

GRADING LAST WEEK
I said that if Arkansas split Missouri and Texas, the 5 seed was "about right." It split: lost 84-83 to Missouri, beat Texas 78-71. It moves up one line, to a 4, because of the Texas win, and I'm calling that a draw.

I said Queens at West Georgia would settle the ASUN. Queens won 73-70 and is 7-0 in the league. Right.

I called Utah St. the shakiest 2 seed I'd ever put in a bracket. It went 1-2 this week, lost 79-69 at Colorado State, and is 3-4 in the Mountain West. Right, and it drops to a 3.

I said Florida's 2 seed "probably won't last." It lasted. Florida beat Kentucky 88-49, lost at Alabama, and is 3-3 in the SEC with two top-25 wins. Wrong, for now.

I said UCF was one more loss from being out. It lost 86-57 at home to Kansas State and is still in, as a 12. I lied. The bubble beneath it got weaker.

RISERS
North Carolina goes from a 6 to a 3. The Tar Heels beat Boston College 93-58, Louisville 93-57 and Pittsburgh 84-67, and their rating rose from 20th to 12th. Butler goes from the First Four to a 7 after winning 89-56 at Providence, 85-60 at Uconn and 76-54 over Xavier, up 3.5 rating points. Miami goes from an 11 to a 7, with wins over SMU, NC State and Duke. Kansas State goes from a 13 to an 8 after winning 86-57 at UCF. Kansas moves up to the 2 line.

Syracuse is the biggest riser in the country, up 4.1 points and from 67th to 44th. It beat Georgia Tech 110-70, won 86-69 at Duke and 97-58 at California, and comes in as a 10.

FALLERS
Massachusetts lost 79-70 at Kent State and 71-68 to Bowling Green. It still wins the MAC on rating, by 4.7 points, but it falls from a 9 to a 15. New Hampshire lost 70-57 at Massachusetts-Lowell and falls from a 7 to a 12. New Mexico State lost 69-67 at Florida International and falls from an 8 to a 13. Navy lost at American and at Colgate and falls from a 10 to a 14.

IN AND OUT
Out: Uconn, Pacific, San Francisco, NC State, West Virginia, Denver and Abilene Christian. That's seven. Uconn lost at Creighton and to Butler and is 2-5 in the Big East. Pacific lost by 20 to a 4-13 team. San Francisco lost by 32 to Gonzaga and then 59-58 at home to St. Mary's. West Virginia lost three straight and is 2-5 in the Big 12. NC State lost twice by double digits.

In: Syracuse, Arizona, Tennessee, Nebraska, Saint Joseph's, Oral Roberts and Utah Valley. Tennessee won at Kentucky and won 80-79 at Vanderbilt and is 5-2 in the SEC. Nebraska won at USC and at UCLA. Saint Joseph's is 7-0 in the A-10, 10-0 in its last ten, and beat St. Louis 77-54.

Oral Roberts takes the Summit's automatic bid from Denver. The ratings are 0.41 apart, Oral Roberts is 4-0 in the league, and it beat Denver 85-63 on Day 26. That's exactly the case my within-a-point rule was written for. Utah Valley takes the WAC by rating and by sweeping Abilene Christian, 69-63 and 77-62.

UNC Asheville is 7-0 in the Big South and still isn't my automatic bid, because Longwood is rated 2.5 points higher. Last week I said this was the call I'd happily lose. It's starting to look like the call I deserve to lose.

THE BUBBLE
Last four in: West Georgia, Nebraska, Saint Joseph's and Tennessee. First Four Out: Uconn, Liberty, Texas A&M and Grand Canyon. Next Four Out: American, Chattanooga, East Tennessee State and NC State.

Uconn is the name that hurts. It was an 8 seed a week ago and it is still rated 51st. But it is 2-5 in its own league and 5-5 in its last ten, and the four teams I put ahead of it are all winning. Liberty has three bad losses. Texas A&M is 5-1 in the SEC and rated 67th, and it needs one good win.

THE PATTERN: THE CEILING HAS TEETH
The new engine has been running for two full weeks, and here is the honest scorecard. Upsets of 20 or more points by my ratings: two in the last week of the old engine, nine last week, fourteen this week. Five of this week's were by 30 or more. The ceiling is doing what you asked for. Tier S teams still went 53-16, and only 11 games were decided by 40 or more. And 65 games were decided by three points or fewer.

My take: blowouts are gone, and that's good. The upsets are real now, but on Day 27 alone a 5-12 team beat Florida State by 15 and a 4-13 team beat Pacific by 20. In real life that happens once a season, not twice in one day. That one's for the commissioner, not the committee.

HOT TAKE
Seton Hall is the least convincing unbeaten team in the country. It is 16-0, rated fifth, with one top-25 win and a schedule rated -0.4. Its Big East wins this week came over Marquette, Xavier and Providence. San Diego State has beaten Utah St. twice. Gonzaga has won three road games by an average of 27. Seton Hall goes to Uconn on Day 28, which used to be a test and isn't anymore. I have it as the top 2 seed, and that's the ceiling until it beats somebody.

A HYPOTHETICAL
Say the committee threw out the five results this week that were 30-point upsets or worse. Florida State is 16-0 and has an argument for the top line. New Hampshire, New Orleans and Pacific are unbeaten in their leagues. Massachusetts is still in trouble, because it also lost at Kent State. Five freak results touched a 2 seed, two automatic bids and a team that just fell out of the field. That's the cost of chaos. It's also why you play the games.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 28: Texas at Vanderbilt, Florida State at Duke, Baylor at Kansas, Seton Hall at Uconn. Day 29: Pepperdine at Gonzaga, Iowa at Illinois, Utah St. at UNLV, Vanderbilt at Missouri. Day 30: San Diego State at UNLV, Texas at Missouri, North Carolina at Virginia, Memphis at UAB, Kansas at Iowa St. Day 31: Missouri at Florida, Pittsburgh at Florida State.

The one I care about most is Texas: Vanderbilt on Day 28, Missouri on Day 30. Win both and the 1 seed is earned. Lose either and Seton Hall or Florida gets the argument.

season-2.headline: Week 10: Texas Falls Off the Top Line, Creighton Ends Seton Hall's Perfect Season, and UNC Asheville Finally Gets Its Bid
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Thirty days and 3,568 games are in, 467 of them since the last bracket. Three unbeaten teams are left: San Diego State (20-0), Gonzaga (19-0) and Iowa (18-0). Seton Hall is no longer one of them, and if you read last week's column you saw that coming.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Texas lost at Vanderbilt and at Missouri and falls off the top line. Missouri went 3-0, beat Vanderbilt and Texas, and leads the SEC at 9-1. Utah St. won three games by a combined 95 points. Creighton, 8-11, won 71-66 at Seton Hall.

Not big: Texas A&M-Corpus Christi, 3-16, beat New Orleans 57-55, a 35.4-point upset by my ratings and the biggest of the week. It cost New Orleans a seed line and nothing else.

GRADING LAST WEEK
I called Seton Hall the least convincing unbeaten team in the country. On Day 29 it won 76-75 at Creighton. On Day 30 Creighton came to Seton Hall and won 71-66, a 32.9-point upset by the ratings. I'll take that one, even if Creighton did most of the work.

I said Texas needed to win at Vanderbilt and at Missouri to keep its 1 seed, and that losing either would hand the argument to Seton Hall or Florida. Texas lost both, 74-59 and 79-65. Florida went 3-0, all on the road. Seton Hall lost to Creighton. So the argument went to somebody I didn't name.

I said UCF was still in because the bubble beneath it got weaker. This week it lost 80-46 at Arizona and 86-63 at Baylor and is out. The bubble finally got tired of carrying it.

And UNC Asheville. Two weeks running I gave the Big South bid to Longwood on rating while the Bulldogs kept winning, and last week I said it was the call I deserved to lose. They're 9-0 in the league, they beat Longwood 83-74, and the ratings are now 1.03 apart. The bid is theirs.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State is the No. 1 overall seed for the third straight week. It beat Colorado State 82-63 and San Jose State 81-65, then won 81-55 at UNLV. Last week I said that trip was the next real chance for the gap at the top to close. It was a 26-point win. The Aztecs are at 52.56 on the Board.

Alabama (18-1) is second at 47.58. It went 3-0, but it needed an 84-82 escape at Texas A&M. Gonzaga (19-0) is third. It beat Pepperdine 95-62 and won 73-39 at Portland.

The fourth 1 seed is Kansas, and I'm overruling my own Board to do it. Texas is still fourth on the Board at 40.21 and Kansas is fifth at 37.36. The Board loves Texas's schedule, rated 10.2, and its three top-25 wins. But Texas is 5-4 in the SEC and 6-4 in its last ten. Kansas is 18-2 and 9-1 in the Big 12, with three top-25 wins and three more over teams in the 26-to-50 range. Kansas lost 81-68 at Iowa St. on Day 30, so this isn't a coronation. It's a team that wins its league beating a team that has lost four of its last ten. Texas is a 2 seed, alongside Missouri, Florida State and Florida.

THREE BIDS CHANGE HANDS
My rule since Week 8 has been that when two teams are within about a point, the standings and head-to-head decide the automatic bid. I'm stretching it to a point and a half. Here's why.

Big East: Georgetown (16-2, 8-0) over Seton Hall (18-1, 8-1). The ratings are 1.29 apart, they don't meet until Days 37 and 38, and Georgetown hasn't lost in the league. Seton Hall is a 3 seed as an at-large. So is Georgetown, as the champion.

Big South: UNC Asheville, as above. Summit: Oral Roberts keeps it. Denver is rated 1.54 points higher, but Oral Roberts is 7-0 and swept Denver, 85-63 at home and 78-73 on the road on Day 30. A team that beat you twice and hasn't lost in the league gets the bid.

SoCon: East Tennessee State over Wofford, on rating alone. Both are 6-2, the ratings are 1.25 apart, and Wofford lost 74-64 at home to UNC Greensboro this week. Wofford falls out entirely and lands in my First Four Out.

RISERS
Utah St. is the scariest 3 seed in the country. Two weeks ago it was the shakiest 2. This week it won 82-62 at Fresno State and 93-53 at UNLV, beat Nevada 85-50, and rose to fifth in the ratings. If the Aggies had beaten San Diego State once, they'd be a 1 seed.

Missouri goes from a 3 to a 2. Wisconsin goes from a 9 to a 6 after beating Oregon, Michigan and Indiana. Purdue goes from a 10 to an 8 and is 8-1 in the Big 10. Liberty comes in as a 10 after going 3-0, including a 71-68 win over New Mexico State. Nebraska won three straight, including 75-68 over Michigan, and moves to a 10.

FALLERS
UNLV went 0-3. It lost 87-77 at Nevada, then lost 93-53 to Utah St. and 81-55 to San Diego State on its own floor. It falls from a 6 to a 9. Illinois also went 0-3, and the last loss, 72-70 at home to Minnesota, was an 18.9-point miss. It falls from a 9 to an 11. St. Louis lost 79-64 at Duquesne, a 22.9-point miss, and falls from a 7 to a 12. North Carolina lost 89-69 at Virginia and drops to a 5. Pepperdine lost at Oregon State and at Gonzaga and drops from a 7 to a 9.

IN AND OUT
In: Liberty, Uconn, Texas A&M, TCU, East Tennessee State and UNC Asheville. Out: Virginia Tech, West Georgia, Tennessee, UCF, Wofford and Longwood.

Virginia Tech lost 76-71 at Stanford and 75-72 at California, two teams outside my top 125. Tennessee is 11-8 with three bad losses. West Georgia lost the ASUN to Queens, and its Board score of 13.64 isn't enough without the bid.

Texas A&M lost to Alabama by two and to Arkansas by seven, and it still moves in, because its schedule is rated 9.0 and the teams around it on the bubble lost to worse teams. Losing close to the best teams in the country isn't a résumé. It just beats losing to California.

THE BUBBLE AND THE HOT TAKE
Last four in: Texas A&M, TCU, Duke and Saint Joseph's. First Four Out: West Virginia, Grand Canyon, Wofford and UCF. Next Four Out: West Georgia, Pacific, Virginia Tech and Tennessee.

Hot take: TCU belongs in over West Virginia, and the Board is wrong about it. West Virginia is 15.46 on the Board and TCU is 13.96. But TCU won 65-64 at West Virginia on Day 28, is 6-4 in the Big 12 to West Virginia's 3-6, and has a top-25 win and a schedule rated 9.95. West Virginia has two bad losses and has lost six of its last ten. When the head-to-head, the standings and the trend all point the same way, I'll take them over a formula.

THE CEILING, ROUND TWO
The chaos rate came down to 1.5% this week, and the scoreboard noticed. Upsets of 20 or more points by my ratings: 14 last week, 5 this week. Upsets of 30 or more: 5 last week, 3 this week. Of the 435 games played at the new rate, four were chaos games. Tier S teams went 45-22. 75 games were decided by three points or fewer, up from 65 last week, and scoring fell to 67.9 a team, against 70.2 for the season. The league is tighter than it has ever been, and the upsets now look like upsets instead of lottery draws.

A HYPOTHETICAL
None of the three unbeaten teams plays a top-25 team for the rest of the regular season. San Diego State has ten games left, Gonzaga eleven, Iowa twelve. If all three win out, all three go into the conference tournaments at 30-0. The committee would then have to decide, with no head-to-head results and no common opponents worth the name, which 30-0 team is the No. 1 overall. My answer today is San Diego State, because it has the toughest schedule of the three by a mile, 9.07 against Gonzaga's 1.78 and Iowa's 3.09. Ask me again in March.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 31: Missouri at Florida, UNLV at San Diego State, Pittsburgh at Florida State, Texas at Texas A&M, Georgetown at Uconn. Day 32: Arkansas at Vanderbilt, Villanova at Seton Hall, VCU at St. Louis, Iowa St. at West Virginia. Day 33: Valparaiso at Bradley, Arkansas at Florida, Kansas at Kansas State. Day 34: Kansas at Arizona, Virginia at Florida State, Texas A&M at Alabama.

My game of the week is Missouri at Florida: the SEC leader against a team that just won three straight on the road. The winner has a real case for a 1 seed if Kansas slips again.

season-2.headline: Week 11: Colorado State Ends San Diego State's Perfect Season, Five Bids Change Hands, and My TCU Take Evaporates
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Thirty-three days and 4,045 games are in, 477 of them since the last bracket. Nine days of regular season are left. Two unbeaten teams remain, Gonzaga (22-0) and Iowa (21-0), because Colorado State beat San Diego State 73-70 on Day 32. Last week I wrote a whole hypothetical about three teams going into the conference tournaments at 30-0. It lasted two days.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: San Diego State's first loss. Florida beat Missouri 79-61 and Arkansas 79-74. Kansas won 86-85 at Kansas State and is 12-1 in the Big 12. Five automatic bids changed hands.

Not big: the week's biggest upset by my ratings was Montana State 71, Sacramento State 61, a 31.3-point miss. It cost Sacramento State the Big Sky bid, which tells you how thin the Big Sky is.

GRADING LAST WEEK
My hot take was TCU over West Virginia, because TCU won the head-to-head, had the better league record and was trending up. TCU then lost 89-51 at Kansas, 89-70 at BYU and 70-69 at Utah, a team rated 245th. It is 12-11 and out. That take didn't age, it evaporated. In my defence, West Virginia went 1-2 and is 4-8 in the Big 12, so it stays out too. Nobody wins this one.

My game of the week was Missouri at Florida, and I said the winner had a case for a 1 seed if Kansas slipped. Florida won by 18. Kansas didn't slip. Then Florida lost 72-69 in overtime at home to Ole Miss two days later, a 23.9-point upset. The 1 seed will keep.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State stays the No. 1 overall seed, loss and all. The Aztecs beat UNLV 86-60, lost at Colorado State, and won 79-56 at Boise State. They're 22-1 with four top-25 wins, the most in the country alongside Florida, and their Board score of 52.86 is still 6.6 points clear of Alabama. One loss on the road to a team rated 43rd doesn't erase that.

Alabama (20-1) beat Georgia 97-72 and South Carolina 94-72. Gonzaga won three home games by 32, 42 and 24 and is 22-0 with a schedule rated 0.96, which is the whole problem with Gonzaga in one number.

Kansas keeps the last 1 seed. Texas went 3-0, won 94-78 at Texas A&M, and now sits just 0.78 ahead of Kansas on the Board, 39.60 to 38.82. Kansas is 12-1 in the Big 12. Texas is 8-4 in the SEC. Both have three top-25 wins. I'm still taking the team that wins its league. The 2 line is Texas, Florida, Florida State and Seton Hall.

FIVE BIDS, ONE RULE
The rule since Week 10: within a point and a half, the standings and the head-to-head decide; beyond that, the rating does. This week it cut both ways.

Big East: Seton Hall takes it back from Georgetown. Seton Hall beat Villanova 95-51 and Providence 85-49 and is now rated 2.61 points higher. Georgetown is 11-0 in the league and Seton Hall 10-1, and I know how that looks. They play at Seton Hall on Day 37 and at Georgetown on Day 38, and that will settle it properly.

Summit: Denver takes it back from Oral Roberts. Oral Roberts swept Denver and is 8-1 in the league, but Denver is now rated 4.97 points higher. Too big a gap.

SoCon: Wofford over East Tennessee State, and this one is clean. Wofford beat ETSU 88-62 on Day 33, is 9-2 to ETSU's 8-3, and is rated two points higher.

Big Sky: Eastern Washington over Sacramento State, on rating. Both are 9-2. Sacramento State lost at home to a 9-13 team.

Big West: Hawaii over UC Irvine. They're 0.08 apart on rating, Hawaii is 10-2 to 8-4, and Hawaii beat Irvine twice, 73-72 and 82-44.

MOVERS
Butler is up from a 7 to a 5 after beating Marquette 83-69 and Uconn 77-68, and it's 10-1 in the Big East. Purdue won three road games and is 11-1 in the Big 10, up to a 7. Nebraska won three straight, by 23, 21 and 37, and is 9-2 in the Big 10.

Pittsburgh went 0-3: 76-48 at Florida State, 75-68 at Boston College, 81-73 at Stanford. It falls from an 8 to an 11 and is one bad week from out. Texas Tech lost at Baylor and at home to Kansas State and drops to a 5. Wisconsin lost to Ohio St. twice in two days and drops from a 6 to a 7. Virginia lost 75-66 at home to 7-14 Georgia Tech, a 27.6-point miss, then beat Duke 84-55. That's the most Virginia week possible, and it costs one line.

IN AND OUT

THE CEILING, WEEK THREE
Ten of this week's 477 games were chaos games, about 2.1%, after four of 435 last week. Over the two weeks at the new rate it's 14 of 912, which is 1.5% on the nose. A HYPOTHETICAL

WHAT TO WATCH

season-2.headline: Week 12: Pacific Ends Gonzaga's Perfect Season, Florida State Takes a 1 Seed, and the Bubble Gets Judged Like a Committee Would
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Thirty-six days and 4,518 games are in, 473 of them since the last bracket. Six days of regular season are left, and the unbeaten list is empty: Pacific beat Gonzaga 78-73 on Day 36, two days after losing to the Bulldogs by 19.

A NOTE ON HOW I'M PICKING
The commissioner told me this week, fairly, that I've been bracketing like a spreadsheet. The automatic-bid rule I invented in Week 8, where a rating gap of a point and a half decided things, is gone. So is any pick that rests on one number. The committee doesn't work that way. It looks at who you beat, where, who you lost to, how you're playing now, and then a human decides. Every bubble call below is a straight comparison: put two résumés side by side and ask which team the room would say is better. The ratings are evidence, not the verdict.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Gonzaga's first loss. Iowa lost 73-59 at Michigan St. and 71-56 at Michigan on back-to-back days. Georgetown went 3-0 and is 14-0 in the Big East. Miami won 86-74 at Virginia. BYU beat Kansas 88-76 and won 80-74 at Iowa St.

Not big: Liberty losing 68-66 at Delaware, a 7-18 team, was a 25.1-point upset by my ratings. It's also exactly what Liberty has done all year, and it's why Liberty is out.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State (24-1) is the No. 1 overall seed. It beat New Mexico 97-59 and Boise State 99-54 and has four top-25 wins. Alabama (23-1) is second after beating Texas A&M by 29, Ole Miss by 15 and Auburn by 56. Gonzaga (24-1) stays on the top line. Losing at Pacific, a team that is now in my field, is the kind of loss the committee forgives.

The fourth 1 seed is Florida State, and Kansas drops to a 2. Kansas needed overtime to win 73-71 at Arizona and then lost 88-76 at BYU. Florida State is 24-1, 14-1 in the ACC, and its only loss came on the road. This week it beat Virginia 83-62 and Notre Dame, then won 70-63 at NC State. Texas has the best case of the teams left off the top line: four top-25 wins against Florida State's three, and a much harder schedule. But Texas has lost four games and Florida State has lost one. When the résumés are that close, the room takes the team that keeps winning.

The 2 line is Texas, Kansas, Georgetown and Florida.

THE BIG EAST BID
Georgetown is my Big East champion. It is 22-2 and 14-0 in the league after beating Uconn 88-52 and winning 86-73 at Marquette and 98-84 at Villanova. Seton Hall is rated a little higher, but it lost 73-61 at home to Butler on Day 34 before winning the rematch 78-60. They play on Day 37 at Seton Hall and Day 38 at Georgetown. Those two games decide the bid, and probably a seed line each.

GRADING LAST WEEK
I said I'd rather face Valparaiso in March than Bradley, the team that had just beaten it. In the rematch on Day 34, Valparaiso won 89-56. I'll be quiet about the Missouri Valley for a while.

I put Iowa at Michigan on the watch list as the Hawkeyes' last real test. Michigan won by 15, and Michigan St. had beaten Iowa by 14 the day before. Iowa is 22-2 and drops from a 3 to a 4.

RISERS AND FALLERS
Miami is up from a 7 to a 4. The Hurricanes beat Virginia Tech 79-55 and Louisville 95-67, won at Virginia, and are 9-1 in their last ten. Michigan is up from an 8 to a 6 after beating Wisconsin and Iowa. Nebraska beat Purdue 79-78, is 12-2 in the Big 10 and moves up to a 7.

Virginia lost by 21 at Florida State and by 12 at home to Miami and drops to an 8. Butler won at Seton Hall, then lost at Xavier and at home to Seton Hall, and drops to a 7. Wisconsin lost at Michigan and 89-58 at Michigan St. and is a 9. Arizona lost to Kansas in overtime and then 74-66 at Utah, a 10-14 team, and is a 10.

IN AND OUT
In: BYU, Michigan St., Pacific, San Jose State and Oklahoma State. Out: Illinois, Villanova, St. Louis, Pittsburgh and Liberty.

BYU is the clearest case for the new approach. It's rated 59th, which the old me would have held against it. It's also 17-7, 10-4 in the Big 12, with three top-25 wins, two of them this week. Two weeks ago TCU had almost exactly BYU's rating and a far worse record, and I put TCU in the field on a head-to-head result. That was the mistake. BYU is a 9 seed.

Michigan St. beat Iowa 73-59 and Wisconsin 89-58 and has won eight of its last ten. Pacific beat Gonzaga. Both are in.

THE BUBBLE, ONE COMPARISON AT A TIME
Last four in: Texas A&M, San Jose State, Saint Joseph's and Oklahoma State. First Four Out: Liberty, Pittsburgh, St. Louis and Illinois. Next Four Out: Villanova, West Virginia, Ole Miss and East Tennessee State.

Oklahoma State or Liberty? Oklahoma State is 18-7, 10-5 in the Big 12, and beat Kansas State 78-68 this week. Liberty is 19-5 with four losses to teams outside my top 100, the latest at Delaware. Oklahoma State.

Saint Joseph's or St. Louis? Saint Joseph's is 20-5 and 13-2 in the A-10 with two wins over top-50 teams. St. Louis is 18-7 and 9-6 and has not beaten a top-50 team all season. Saint Joseph's, and it isn't close.

San Jose State or Pittsburgh? San Jose State has won three straight, beaten a top-25 team and two more in the top 50, and played a schedule rated 9.1. Pittsburgh is 18-6 with no wins over a top-50 team and three bad losses. San Jose State.

Texas A&M or Illinois? Texas A&M is 8-6 in the SEC with a top-25 win and the hardest schedule on the bubble. Illinois is 4-6 in its last ten with three bad losses. Texas A&M.

HOT TAKE
Florida State is the most underrated 1 seed in years, and I mean that as a compliment. Twenty-four wins, one loss, three top-25 wins and three more over top-50 teams, and the only reason anyone argues is a schedule rated 4.0. The Seminoles beat Virginia by 21 this week. Syracuse visits on Day 39. If you want to doubt them, that's your chance.

A HYPOTHETICAL
If Georgetown sweeps Seton Hall on Days 37 and 38, it's 24-2, 16-0 in the Big East, with two more wins over a top-10 team. At that point I'd put Georgetown on the top line ahead of Florida State. If they split, nothing moves. If Seton Hall sweeps, it takes the Big East bid and jumps to a 2.

THE NUMBERS
83 games were decided by three points or fewer this week, the most of any week I've tracked, up from 59. Home teams won 63.6%. Tier S teams went 46-20. Eight of the 473 games were chaos games, close to the 1.5% rate. Only four upsets were of 20 points or more.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 37: Georgetown at Seton Hall, Vanderbilt at Arkansas, San Diego State at Fresno State, Kansas State at BYU. Day 38: Seton Hall at Georgetown, Arkansas at Alabama, Miami at North Carolina, Iowa at Purdue. Day 39: Syracuse at Florida State, Gonzaga at Pepperdine, Baylor at Kansas State.

Game of the week: Arkansas at Alabama on Day 38. Arkansas is 22-2. Alabama is 23-1. One of them leaves with a third loss in a year where losses are getting expensive.

season-2.headline: Week 13: Georgetown Sweeps Seton Hall and Takes a 1 Seed, Gonzaga Drops to the 2 Line, and the Bubble Bites Back
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Thirty-nine days and 4,998 games are in, 480 of them since the last bracket. Three days of regular season remain, then the conference tournaments. This is the last bracket before the automatic bids start being decided on the floor instead of in my head.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Georgetown swept Seton Hall, 86-78 on the road and 96-82 at home, and is 17-0 in the Big East. Alabama beat Arkansas 82-77. Florida State beat Syracuse. Iowa lost twice more. Two of last week's last four in collapsed.

Not big: Binghamton, 5-24, won 77-62 at Maine, the biggest upset of the week by my ratings. Maine isn't anywhere near the field.

A PROMISE KEPT
Last week I wrote that if Georgetown swept Seton Hall, I'd put the Hoyas on the top line ahead of Florida State. They swept them, then beat Marquette 84-82 for good measure. So Georgetown is a 1 seed. What I didn't see coming is who it's replacing.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State (27-1) is the No. 1 overall seed. It won three road games, at Fresno State by 31, at New Mexico and at San Jose State. Alabama (26-1) is second after beating Kentucky, Arkansas and Oklahoma.

Georgetown is third: 25-2, unbeaten in the league, three top-25 wins, seven more over top-50 teams, and a schedule rated 9.4. That's the deepest résumé in the country outside San Diego State.

The fourth 1 seed is Florida State, and the team that drops to a 2 is Gonzaga. Last week I called Florida State the most underrated 1 seed in years and told you Syracuse on Day 39 was your chance to doubt it. Florida State won 67-55 and is 27-1. Gonzaga is also 27-1 and won all three this week. Here's the comparison the committee makes: Florida State has three top-25 wins and four more over top-50 teams. Gonzaga has two and three. Florida State's schedule is rated 4.7, Gonzaga's 2.5. Gonzaga's ratings are better because it beats bad teams by more, and that isn't nothing. But when two 27-1 teams are side by side, the room takes the one that has beaten more good teams. Gonzaga leads the 2 line with Texas, Florida and Missouri.

Texas deserves a sentence. It won at Georgia, Kentucky and South Carolina by 35, 11 and 41, has four top-25 wins and is 9-1 in its last ten. It hosts Alabama on Day 41. Win that and Texas is in the top-line argument again.

GRADING LAST WEEK
Game of the week was Arkansas at Alabama. Alabama won by five. Arkansas also lost 75-66 at home to Vanderbilt and is now 23-4. It stays on the 4 line because its wins are real.

The bubble comparisons went badly for two of my picks. Saint Joseph's, which I took over St. Louis, lost all three games, the last 73-53 at home to a 9-18 St. Bonaventure team. Texas A&M, which I took over Illinois, lost by 35 at Florida and at South Carolina. Both are out. St. Louis lost twice too, so at least the comparison was right about St. Louis. San Jose State, the third of the four, beat Boise State and won at Nevada and stays in.

THE AUTOMATIC BIDS
A projected automatic bid is the team I think wins the conference tournament. Two change this week.

Big 10: Purdue over Iowa. Iowa has lost four of its last seven, including 72-58 at Indiana and 73-71 in overtime at Purdue. Purdue is 14-3, tied for the league lead with Nebraska, and beat Iowa head to head. Iowa is still the better team on paper and is a 5 seed. But if you asked me who's cutting down the nets in the Big 10 tournament, I'd say Purdue.

Horizon: Detroit Mercy over Oakland. Detroit Mercy leads the league by two and a half games. Oakland lost at home to 9-18 Northern Kentucky.

MOVERS
North Carolina is up from a 5 to a 3. It won at NC State, beat Miami 90-76 and won at Boston College, and is 14-3 in the ACC. Wisconsin won three straight and moves to a 7. Duke beat Stanford, Notre Dame and Miami and moves from an 11 to an 8. BYU won three more, at West Virginia and Oklahoma State and over Kansas State, and is 13-4 in the Big 12.

Miami lost at North Carolina and at Duke and drops from a 4 to a 6. Marquette lost three straight, by one at DePaul, by one at home to Villanova and by two at Georgetown, and falls from an 8 into the First Four. Pepperdine lost at home to Seattle, a 10-18 team, and falls from a 9 to the First Four.

IN AND OUT
In: Ole Miss, Villanova, West Virginia and Detroit Mercy. Out: Texas A&M, Saint Joseph's, Oklahoma State and Oakland.

Ole Miss is the interesting one. It's 16-11, and normally a record like that doesn't get in. But it has three top-25 wins and a schedule rated 10.7, and it just beat Vanderbilt twice in two days. When the committee lines up the résumés, Ole Miss has more top-25 wins than anyone else near the bubble. It's a 10 seed.

THE BUBBLE, ONE COMPARISON AT A TIME
Last four in: Marquette, Pepperdine, Pacific and West Virginia. First Four Out: Uconn, Pittsburgh, Texas A&M and Oklahoma State. Next Four Out: Saint Joseph's, St. Louis, Liberty and Davidson.

Marquette or Uconn? Same league. Marquette is 19-8 and 10-7. Uconn is 18-10 and 8-10, and its three-game win streak was against St. John's and Providence twice. Marquette's three losses came by a combined four points. Marquette.

West Virginia or Pittsburgh? West Virginia is 7-11 in the Big 12 and I've kept it out for weeks. But it has two top-25 wins and three more over top-50 teams, and it just beat Texas Tech by 14. Pittsburgh is 20-7 with one win over a top-50 team all season. The committee takes the team that has beaten good teams. West Virginia, barely.

Pacific or Uconn? Pacific beat Gonzaga and is 13-4 in its league. Pacific.

Pepperdine is the shakiest team in my field. It lost at home to Seattle and has three bad losses. It's in on the strength of a top-25 win and a schedule rated 6.9, and Uconn is right behind it.

HOT TAKE
Colorado State is the team nobody wants in its region. It has won ten straight, it's 13-5 in the Mountain West, and it beat San Diego State. It's a 10 seed. A 1 seed drawing Colorado State in the second round would be the worst draw in the bracket.

A HYPOTHETICAL
Alabama plays at Florida on Day 40 and at Texas on Day 41. If it loses both, it's 26-3, and I'd look hard at Texas and Gonzaga for its spot. If it wins both, Alabama has the best two-day stretch of anyone's season and a real case for the No. 1 overall over San Diego State.

THE NUMBERS
Six of the 480 games were chaos games, a shade over 1%. 65 games were decided by three points or fewer and 11 went to overtime. Tier S teams went 50-18.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 40: Alabama at Florida, North Carolina at Florida State, Seton Hall at Marquette, West Virginia at Arizona, San Jose State at Colorado State. Day 41: Alabama at Texas, Butler at Marquette, Duke at Pittsburgh, Uconn at Seton Hall. Day 42: Georgetown at Butler, Pittsburgh at Miami, Marquette at Villanova, Nebraska at Wisconsin.

Game of the week: Alabama at Texas on Day 41. A 1 seed is probably riding on it, and maybe two.

season-2.headline: Week 14: Alabama Wins the Game of the Year, DePaul Stuns Georgetown, and Ole Miss Becomes Everyone's Nightmare
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. The regular season is over: 5,475 games, 477 of them in the last three days. Next come five days of conference tournaments, then the real field. This is my last bracket built on projection. Next time, the automatic bids will be decided on the floor.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Alabama lost at Florida and then won 106-104 in overtime at Texas, the game of the year. DePaul, 7-23, beat Georgetown 65-61 in Georgetown's own building. Ole Miss beat Arkansas and is now the most dangerous team outside the top six lines. Colorado State finished on a 12-game winning streak.

Not big: almost everything else. The top of the bracket held, and the bubble mostly settled.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State is the No. 1 overall seed for the seventh straight week. It finished 29-1 by beating Air Force by 49 and Nevada by 49. The Aztecs have been the best team in this league since Week 8, and they finish as the clear top seed.

Alabama is second. Last week I said that if it won at Florida and at Texas, it had a case for the No. 1 overall. It split, losing 91-81 at Florida and winning that overtime classic at Texas, then won at Auburn. At 28-2 with five top-25 wins, tied for the most in the country, it is a very comfortable 1 seed.

Florida State is third: 29-1, 19-1 in the ACC, and it beat North Carolina 81-61. It now has four top-25 wins and four more over top-50 teams.

THE FOURTH 1 SEED
This is the closest call in the bracket, and here is the comparison.

Georgetown is 27-3 and won the Big East by four games. It has four top-25 wins, five more over top-50 teams, and a schedule rated 9.0. It also lost at home to a 7-23 DePaul team, a 39.9-point upset by my ratings and the second-biggest since the realism ceiling arrived.

Florida is 26-4. It has five top-25 wins, including Alabama this week, and a schedule rated 9.1. It finished third in the SEC.

Gonzaga is 29-1 with two top-25 wins and a schedule rated 2.5.

I'm keeping Georgetown, by a hair. Nine wins over top-50 teams and an outright league title outweigh one terrible night. Florida is the first team on the 2 line and one good SEC tournament from passing it. Gonzaga, Texas and Missouri complete the 2 line.

GRADING LAST WEEK
Game of the week was Alabama at Texas, and I said a 1 seed might ride on it. It went to overtime, 106-104, and it decided that Texas would stay a 2.

My hot take was that Colorado State was the team nobody wanted in their region. It won twice more, both over San Jose State, and finishes on 12 straight. It's a 9 seed now and still nobody's preferred draw.

Ole Miss, the 16-11 team I talked myself into last week, went 3-0. It beat Kentucky by 30, Oklahoma by 39 and Arkansas by 11, has four top-25 wins, and rises from a 10 to a 7.

THE AUTOMATIC BIDS
These are my picks to win each conference tournament. Two change.

SoCon: UNC Greensboro, the regular-season champion at 14-4. Wofford is rated higher, but it finished fourth in the league. I'm taking the team that won the league.

SWAC: Bethune-Cookman. Arkansas-Pine Bluff lost its last three games and finished a game behind.

Everything else holds. The Big 10 goes to Purdue, regular-season champion at 16-4. The Big 12 is a dead heat between Kansas and Iowa St., both 17-3. I'm sticking with Kansas, but Iowa St. went 3-0 with a win at Texas Tech, has ten wins over top-50 teams, and is the better bet to win the tournament. Both are 3 seeds either way.

MOVERS
Miami is up from a 6 to a 4 after beating Stanford, California and Pittsburgh. Marquette is up from an 11 to an 8 after beating Seton Hall 89-77 and Butler 70-53.

Butler went the other way: 0-3, losing by 25 at St. John's, at Marquette, and at home to Georgetown. It falls from a 6 to a 9 and has lost five of its last ten. UNLV lost 71-50 at Boise State and drops to a 7. Iowa lost at home to Rutgers and UCLA and is a 6, after sitting on the 3 and 4 lines for most of the last month.

IN AND OUT
In: Pittsburgh, Texas A&M, UNC Greensboro and Bethune-Cookman. Out: Arizona, San Jose State, Wofford and Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

Arizona collapsed. It lost its last three, including 84-54 at home to West Virginia, and went 2-8 in its last ten. San Jose State lost all three, twice to Colorado State.

THE BUBBLE, ONE COMPARISON AT A TIME
Last four in: Pittsburgh, Villanova, Pepperdine and Texas A&M. First Four Out: Oklahoma State, Uconn, Arizona and San Jose State. Next Four Out: Illinois, UCLA, Liberty and Oregon.

Pittsburgh or Uconn? Pittsburgh is 22-8, 12-8 in the ACC, and beat Duke this week. Uconn is 19-11 and 9-11 in its league. Pittsburgh.

Villanova or Arizona? Villanova beat Marquette on the final day and is 12-8 in the Big East. Arizona has lost eight of its last ten. Villanova.

Pepperdine or San Jose State? Pepperdine won three road games. San Jose State lost three. Pepperdine.

Texas A&M or Oklahoma State is the hard one. Texas A&M is 18-12 with a schedule rated 10.9, 11-9 in the SEC, and won at Kentucky. Oklahoma State is 20-10 with one more win over a top-50 team, but it lost at home to a UCF team that went 6-14 in the Big 12. I'll take the team that survived the tougher league. If Oklahoma State wins two games in the Big 12 tournament, it passes Texas A&M.

HOT TAKE
Ole Miss is the most dangerous 7 seed I can remember. Four top-25 wins, three straight blowouts, and a schedule rated 10.5. A 2 seed that draws Ole Miss in the second round should be furious.

A HYPOTHETICAL
If Florida wins the SEC tournament, probably by beating Alabama again, and Georgetown loses early in the Big East tournament, Florida is a 1 seed. If Georgetown wins the Big East, the question doesn't come up. The fourth 1 seed will be decided on the floor next week, which is how it should be.

THE NUMBERS
Eighteen games went to overtime this week, the most of any week this season. 70 were decided by three points or fewer. Five of the 477 games were chaos games. Tier S teams went 52-18.

A LOOK BACK
My preseason bracket had Utah St. on the top line. Utah St. finished 24-6 and is a 3 seed. Alabama held the overall No. 1 for seven weeks and San Diego State for the last seven. Kentucky was in and out of my field twice by Week 4 and never came back. Fourteen weeks, a lot of takes, and a few that aged badly. That's bracketology.

WHAT'S NEXT
Conference tournaments run Days 43 to 47. Once the commissioner builds the field after Day 47, I'll file Bracketology HQ's entry in the bracket challenge before the First Four tips off on Day 48. Bring your bracket.
